name: Reformism
summary: Reformism holds that capitalist society can be transformed, or at least made far more just, by gradual change through existing democratic institutions rather than revolution. In its classic socialist form (Bernstein's evolutionary socialism) universal suffrage, trade unions, cooperatives and municipal enterprise are the levers; in its later social-democratic form it stresses welfare, regulation and Keynesian management of a mixed economy. It rejects collapse theories, the dictatorship of the proletariat and vanguard politics.
scope: Reformist socialism and social democracy in the line of Eduard Bernstein's Evolutionary Socialism (1899), with later strands such as Crosland's revisionism and the Godesberg Programme. It excludes the generic sense of reform within any institution, centre-right reformism, and revolutionary socialists who use reforms tactically. Modern social issues are inferred from the centre-left mainstream and given low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Eduard Bernstein
keyFigures.role: German Social Democrat whose Evolutionary Socialism and revisionism founded reformist socialist theory.

keyFigures.name: Anthony Crosland
keyFigures.role: British Labour thinker whose The Future of Socialism argued nationalisation mattered less under Keynesian management.

sources.usedFor: Definition, strands, Crosland, Godesberg, distinction from revolutionary socialism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Welfare provision and social reform are the stock in trade of reformist social democracy, and universal public health care is its standard example.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Reformists seek to improve workers' conditions through legislation, and wage floors are a typical labour-protection measure, though Bernstein stressed unions and arbitration more than statute.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Bernstein defended organisation over anarchic competition but never abolished markets; a modern reformist accepts markets yet doubts they beat governments across the board.

public-ownership.rationale: Bernstein wanted municipalities to run monopoly-type enterprises, while Crosland held nationalisation matters less once Keynesian management exists, so adherents split on major industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Reformists use progressive taxation to spread wealth, and Bernstein favoured shifting tax burdens off small producers, though no source here gives a forceful call for far higher rates.

unions-good.rationale: Bernstein calls trade unions 'indispensable organs of the democracy' and reformism historically rests on the labour movement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bernstein places natural resources 'in the last instance' with the nation and supports expropriation by lawful means, so property is not beyond override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Reformists aim to tame capitalism through regulation and economic management rather than abolish it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social reform and welfare provision are core reformist aims, so cutting welfare as dependency-creating is rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Bernstein judged productive cooperatives the weakest form of associated labour while praising consumer cooperatives, so universal worker ownership is not a reformist demand.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Bernstein's liberal heritage and stress on equal rights implies wariness of state surveillance, but the issue is anachronistic and adherents vary.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Reformism as a tendency has no drug policy; social democrats are divided between liberal and public-health-restrictive views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not an issue the ideology addresses; centre-left reformists are split between speech liberties and protecting minorities.

strong-leader.rationale: Bernstein's democracy means no class government and lawful parliamentary change, so a leader bypassing gridlock contradicts it.

state-harmful.rationale: Reformists work through the state and its democratic institutions and treat strengthened self-government as the route to socialism.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the centre-left reformist habit of using legislation to solve social problems; the ideology has no stated gun doctrine.

empower-police-military.rationale: Bernstein wanted standing armies converted to citizen armies and military courts abolished, implying no appetite for more military authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; contemporary reformists are divided between decriminalisation and abolitionist views.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from reformism's belief that social conditions can be improved by gradual institutional change; no source addresses prisons directly.

traditional-family.rationale: Reformism has no family doctrine; modern social-democratic parties mostly favour pluralism over a privileged traditional family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for Bernstein; modern reformist centre-left parties mostly support it on equal-rights grounds.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the classical texts; modern reformist parties generally support legal access.

more-religion-public.rationale: Reformists generally lean secular and Bernstein's appeal is to Kant and reason, though the ideology itself is silent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from reformist commitment to equal rights and social reform; not a documented core issue.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Outside the ideology's concerns; adherents hold varied views.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bernstein said the worker has a fatherland while remaining a citizen of the world; preservation of culture itself is not a reformist theme.

gradual-change.rationale: Bernstein argues that socialism comes through gradual lawful development, and that cooperatives and institutions 'cannot be produced by magic'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from internationalist labour heritage; contemporary reformist parties are divided, with some favouring restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bernstein wanted social democracy to work for peace and arbitration, which implies support for international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Bernstein discussed tariffs mainly as aids to cartels and did not take a doctrinal line; reformists differ between free-trade and protective camps.

nation-first.rationale: Bernstein held internationalism does not mean yielding to foreign claims but also called for peace and arbitration, so putting the nation ahead of global cooperation is not accepted.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Bernstein defended colonial conquest only conditionally; reformists today are split on intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred; reformist labour movements favoured orderly migration and rarely open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Reformism relies on growth to fund social reform; degrowth is a later green position, not a reformist one.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Modern reformist parties back strong climate policy through legislation, but this is an inference since classical texts predate the issue.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Reformists value progress but offer no doctrine of technological salvation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Reformist parties are split on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bernstein says universal franchise is the alternative to violent revolution and that socialists should use lawful means.

experts-over-public.rationale: Crosland-style economic management leans technocratic but democracy is central; adherents are split.

central-planning.rationale: Bernstein argued the state could not even take over all medium and large enterprises and did not envisage centrally planned economies.

socialized-markets.rationale: Bernstein's mix of consumer cooperatives, municipal enterprise and private firms coexisting fits markets with public or cooperative ownership, but the statement is only loosely tied.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a reformist tenet; this is a Georgist idea and reformists would use varied tax tools.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Redistributive taxation is typical of reformist social democracy, though inheritance tax is inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Reformists are divided between universal basic income and conditional welfare; Bernstein preferred organisational rights over state guarantees.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Bernstein saw tariffs as aggravating cartels, but no firm doctrine; adherents differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic management is a reformist tool, yet Bernstein cautioned about the state's limits; adherents are split on directing investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Bernstein observed that property was spreading among many small and medium owners and approved of that, but did not call for it as a goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bernstein rejected catastrophic transformation and preached gradual improvement within existing economic forms.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Reformist economic management relies on central institutions; abolition is foreign to it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bernstein proposed labour bureaus with equal representation of workers and employers and compulsory arbitration courts, partly compatible, but binding wage and price setting is not central.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bernstein defined democracy as the absence of class government and attacked the dictatorship of the proletariat.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Reformists generally prefer republican democracy, but constitutional monarchy is accepted in many reformist parties.

democracy-best.rationale: Bernstein treats democracy and socialism as inseparable, with democracy the means and substance of change.

direct-votes.rationale: Reformists work through parliament; Bernstein favoured self-government but did not make direct legislation central.

workers-councils.rationale: Bernstein dismissed class dictatorship and relied on parliamentary and local democratic institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; reformists generally favour keeping democratic states intact.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bernstein's democracy rests on equal rights for all members of the community.

political-violence-never.rationale: Bernstein urged lawful means suited to civilisation, but he did not state an absolute pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Reformist social democracy championed peace and arbitration.

separate-church-state.rationale: Reformist parties generally accept secular states, but the ideology has no stated doctrine.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Reformism's democratic and rationalist character, with Bernstein appealing to Kant, rules out scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Reformists want strong public institutions and no privatisation of basic state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Bernstein favoured citizen armies and peace through arbitration over military superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bernstein's equal-rights democracy and citizenship ideals point away from ethnic definitions of the nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bernstein said society had not polarized as the Manifesto described and treated reforms as a counter-movement to class conflict, though classes still matter.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Reformists seek to reduce inequality but typically stop short of full equality of outcome; Crosland stressed equality but with limits.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Bernstein held that cultivation gives title to land and wanted natives treated well, but classical reformism has no doctrine on indigenous authority and modern adherents differ.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Bernstein allowed colonial acquisition if natives were well treated; reparations are not addressed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Reformism has no such doctrine and favours democratic internationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Reformism stresses association and social reform over self-interest as a moral principle.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Bernstein stressed equal rights limiting majority rule and a liberal inheritance.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Reformism is a strategy of social change with no settled position on nature's intrinsic value; green social democrats say yes, others stress human welfare.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; reformism leans against coercive population policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Reformism builds on industrial society and aims to improve it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Reformism favours stability and gradualism over disruptive acceleration.

human-enhancement.rationale: The question is far from reformist concerns and adherents have no common line, treating it as a regulatory matter for democratic debate.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from commitment to democratic accountability.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No reformist source covers it; centre-left parties divide between privacy rights and security-based access.

restore-past-order.rationale: Reformism is forward-looking and seeks progress through reforms rather than restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bernstein said the movement means everything and the final aim little, a pragmatic stance, but reformists still keep principles.

direct-action.rationale: Reformists seek change through elections, parliament and lawful organisations.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bernstein argued that lawful democratic means suit a democratic society and revolution cannot build organic creations.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Reformism aims to improve industrial society through legislation and organisation, so abandoning it for foraging is wholly alien.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Bernstein worked with an industrial economy of differentiated firms and cooperatives and wanted gradual improvement of it, not abolition of its structure.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Reformism favours welfare and equity but keeps the existing mixed economy.

production-for-use.rationale: Reformists accept markets and profit alongside social provision.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Bernstein rejected the Marxist value theory as scientific foundation and observed property spreading.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bernstein called class dictatorship outdated and belonging to a lower civilisation.

collective-farming.rationale: Bernstein supported cooperatives and peasant property protection, not forced collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Bernstein held capitalism could adapt and colonies posed little threat, rejecting inevitability theses.

taxation-theft.rationale: Reformism funds social reform through taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Reformism has no stated position; liberal heritage supports but social-democratic paternalism adds restrictions.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Bernstein called socialism organising liberalism and limited majority rule by equal rights, but he also valued associations.

conscription.rationale: Bernstein preferred citizen armies and shorter service, with no enthusiasm for compulsion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Bernstein made the vote the main lever of change.

state-as-business.rationale: Reformists see the state as a provider of public services, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Reformists hold freedom needs material means; welfare provision and social reform rest on that idea.

media-academia-power.rationale: Reformists place political power in elected parliaments and treat it as accountable to voters, so the claim that media and universities outweigh them is not theirs.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Bernstein's equal-rights democracy opposes racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Bernstein relied on parliamentary democracy though praised trade unions.

total-state.rationale: Bernstein warned against bureaucracy and centralised uniformity.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a reformist theme; gradualism opposes radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Reformist peace and arbitration policy opposes expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Bernstein's democracy is the absence of class government.

bound-labor.rationale: Bernstein's democracy rests on equal rights for all members of the community and on removing feudal remnants, which excludes bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Bernstein appealed to Kant and science, so scepticism about neutral knowledge is not a reformist theme.

universal-morality.rationale: Bernstein's 'Kant against cant' appeals to universal ethical standards.

single-common-good.rationale: Reformists accept competing interests balanced democratically.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Reformism as such takes no stand; social-democratic parties have historically differed over Zionism and Israeli policy.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Reformism has no doctrine of diaspora return and adherents split along national lines.

revive-national-language.rationale: National language revival is a nationalist cause that reformism neither pursues nor opposes in principle.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Bernstein supported democratic organisation and equal worker-employer representation, and later reformists back co-determination.

school-vouchers.rationale: Reformists favour public provision of education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Keynesian economic management is part of reformism; Crosland relied on it.

economic-freedom.rationale: Reformists argue democracy and socialism stand together, not that political freedom depends on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Reformism puts its trust in laws, parliament and organised institutions as the lawful means suited to civilisation, not in rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Reformism favours democratic self-government and nations as a political framework.

force-without-un.rationale: Reformists emphasise peace, arbitration and international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bernstein's appeal to Kant and scientific socialism implies a rationalist outlook though not stated as exclusive.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Reformists tend toward inclusive provision though divided in practice.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Centre-left reformists are split between conditionality and unconditional support.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bernstein proposed labour bureaus with equal worker-employer representation, yet reformists rest on labour organisation and class interests.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Reformists seek gradual improvement while preserving institutions, so destroying cultural heritage for novelty is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Bernstein urged peace and arbitration and cooperation, and reformist parties tend to prefer multilateral cooperation to bloc confrontation with the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Bernstein said the worker has a fatherland yet remains a citizen of the world, so neither purely national nor purely international.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Reformism rests on equal rights before the law, from which modern adherents infer rejection of legally fixed gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Credit is accepted in a reformist mixed economy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Bernstein defined democracy by equal rights for every member of the community, which segregation law violates.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Bernstein defined democracy as the absence of class government, implying the state can be shaped by the majority.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred; modern reformists lean to energy transition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Reformist parties are split between integration with cultural pluralism and expectations of assimilation, and no source settles it.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory about elites and immigration has no basis in reformism, which accepts democratic politics and equal membership.

proportional-representation.rationale: Reformist parties often favour PR to widen democracy, but not doctrinal.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Modern reformist feminists accept it, but not classical doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Reformists work within institutions and trust them.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Bernstein's equal rights and liberal inheritance exclude coercive state interference in reproduction, though early social reformers sometimes flirted with eugenics.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Reformism exists to use the state for social reform, welfare and economic management, far beyond defence and property protection.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal rights for all members of the community leave no room for discouraging marriage across racial lines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Bernstein's democracy rests on equal rights for all members.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Bernstein held social democracy can advance nation by nation through democratic reform.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The classification of settler states is not a reformist doctrine, and Bernstein himself defended colonial acquisition if natives were well treated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Reformism has no stated line on religious personal law; equal rights suggests sympathy but adherents differ.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restricting conversion conflicts with the liberal heritage and equal individual rights that Bernstein attributed to democratic socialism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious dietary bans are not part of reformist programmes, which are built on secular social reform.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Reformists have no common line on religious instruction in state schools; practice varies by country.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bernstein grounds legitimacy in universal franchise and majority rule limited by equal rights.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surpluses are not part of reformism, and Bernstein's internationalism favours peaceful exchange without a zero-sum goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring a minority to leave violates the equal rights that Bernstein's democracy requires.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Bernstein rejected violent revolution but accepted legal expropriation, which libertarian absolutism would call force.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Reformists split between militant democracy and free speech.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican non-domination is not a stated reformist concept, though it fits the stress on organisation against arbitrary power.

separated-powers.rationale: Bernstein supported limits on majorities through equal rights and local self-government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bernstein denied revolutionary preparations and relied on the working class's legal organisations.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Welfare and social reform imply priority for those in need.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Social-democratic parties are split on selling public housing; some see it as widening ownership, others as eroding public provision.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Bernstein called unions indispensable, though he warned against monopoly unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Reformists blame social institutions and seek to improve them.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Reformists rest on equal membership in democracy and do not hold that diversity undermines cohesion, though some centre-left voices stress integration.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Bernstein's democracy is representative and electoral, with universal franchise as the lever, so lotteries are not part of the programme.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bernstein limited majorities by equal rights.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Reformists use regulation but have no doctrine on price ceilings, and economists in the tradition caution about shortages.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bernstein cast socialism as organising liberalism extending individual freedom, which excludes party control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Bernstein preferred citizen armies under democratic control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Equal rights and citizenship lean reformists toward moderate waiting periods, though centre-left parties differ and no source sets a length.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay parity for representatives is a Marxist demand from the Commune; reformist parties have not adopted it as doctrine.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Social-democratic parties value discipline, but reformists defend parliamentary independence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Reformist social democrats are pro-EU in the Party of European Socialists.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Reformists favour parliamentary government and democratic control of the army, as in Bernstein's call for citizen armies and reformed military courts.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside reformist concern; the matter is left to churches under secular law.

clerical-rule.rationale: Bernstein defines democracy as the absence of class government with equal rights for all, which rule by religious scholars denies.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Bernstein said workers have a fatherland and refused to abandon national interests.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Reformism's liberal inheritance and view of socialism as extending freedom oppose censorship of art on moral grounds.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Reformists favour parliamentary government with regular elections and have no interest in removing presidential limits.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Social democrats split on alliances such as NATO; reformism as a doctrine supplies no line beyond peace and arbitration.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Bernstein wanted gradual change and municipal and cooperative provision alongside private ownership, so banning renting is far from reformism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bernstein proposed converting standing armies to citizen armies, a militia-style goal.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Reformism is rooted in the industrial labour movement, and Bernstein sought to improve rural conditions rather than idealise them.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reformism has no doctrine of reunification, which depends on national circumstances.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Reformist movements have drawn heavily on intellectuals and expertise, so adherents reject treating the educated as out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Reformism has no cultural theory; Bernstein defended colonial acquisition if natives were well governed, while modern adherents mostly accept cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Centre-left reformists mostly oppose, though not doctrinal.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Modern centre-left reformist parties support gender equality and sex education in schools, though classical texts say nothing.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Bernstein's appeal to Kant and science as the basis of socialist thought makes creationism in public schools unacceptable.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Reformist parties have no line on pornography and divide between liberal and protective positions.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Equal citizenship favours territorial or open routes.

minority-language-support.rationale: Equal rights for all members of the community suggest support for minority language provision, though classical reformism is silent.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions pit equal application of law against religious liberty, and reformism has no settled doctrine.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: This is a Millian position on conformity; reformism's liberal inheritance is sympathetic but never took it up.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Reformists differ, with development-oriented social democrats favouring relief and fiscal moderates favouring repayment.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The claim belongs to anticolonial socialism; reformism has not taken it up and Bernstein approved of colonial administration done well.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Reformists work through existing institutions, but a democratically elected assembly would be acceptable if constitutional change were wanted.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Democracy and universal franchise are, for Bernstein, the means of progress and not to be suspended for economic ends.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Peace and arbitration and social reform inferred toward international solidarity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Social democratic parties are divided on nuclear weapons, and reformism has no doctrine on them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Reformists have no common stance on presidential versus parliamentary head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Keynesian economic management favours government control, but centre-left parties have accepted independent banks, so adherents split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Bernstein's emphasis on peace and arbitration points toward negotiated territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Bernstein placed natural resources with the nation and supported expropriation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Reformists reject the Soviet model but have no doctrine of defining it as state capitalism, which is a particular left-communist thesis.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Reformists back environmental regulation but have no doctrine on acting under uncertainty.

collective-defense.rationale: Social democrats have both supported and criticised alliances such as NATO, so reformism as such is neutral.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Bernstein criticised how the Kiautschou lease was obtained yet defended it, and reformism has no clear rule on annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Reformism has not pursued anticlerical state control as doctrine, and parties vary by national tradition.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Reformist parties accept both republics and constitutional monarchies with ceremonial heads, with no doctrinal line.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Reformism has no doctrine and parties differ by national setting.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Bernstein valued municipal and regional self-government, but a one country, two systems arrangement is not a reformist theme.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Bernstein defines democracy as the absence of class government and equal rights, which excludes a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation is a reformist tool.

character-from-environment.rationale: Bernstein thought social conditions could be improved through reform, implying circumstances shape people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bernstein's democracy limits even majority rule by equal rights, so a ruler above the law is rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not reformist concern, and adherents have no shared line.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Reformists favour parliamentary democracy and have not adopted mixed-constitution theory.

leader-cult.rationale: Cults of personality contradict the democratic, parliamentary character of reformism.

equal-parenting.rationale: Reformist parties have no common line on shared custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Bernstein denied the dictatorship of the proletariat and a polarised class struggle, so the theory of continuing struggle under socialism is foreign.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bernstein supported protecting peasants and cooperatives rather than expropriating estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Reformists have no settled doctrine on return rights for descendants, and views are context dependent.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Bernstein favoured peace and arbitration and rejected pursuing foreign claims by force, which opposes irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy contradicts the liberal inheritance and equal rights in Bernstein's democracy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes contradict the individual liberty reformism inherits from liberalism.

common-currency.rationale: Reformist social democrats in the Party of European Socialists have backed the euro, though classical texts predate it.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Reformism has no pan-ethnic unification programme and favours democratic internationalism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: This Austro-Marxist idea was available to social democrats but reformism has no settled position.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Bernstein emphasised winning rights within existing states.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bernstein questioned strict historic necessity and economic determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Bernstein held cartels can moderate crises and denied their abolition would help.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic management and stabilising capitalism imply willingness to support failing institutions to protect employment.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Bernstein limited majorities by equal rights.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Modern reformist parties have adopted gender quotas, but classical texts say nothing.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Bernstein's world-market analysis and internationalism are incompatible with autarkic blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from reformism's emphasis on labour protection through law and arbitration, extended to trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Reformists keep wage labour and material incentives and seek to improve them, not replace them with moral incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Bernstein rejected violent seizure of power and held that stages of development cannot be skipped.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bernstein presented socialism as liberalism's heir against feudal remnants.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Reformism has no doctrine on history teaching and adherents differ.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Bernstein allowed colonial rule if natives treated well and cultivated land.

patriotic-education.rationale: Bernstein affirmed workers' fatherland, but not school patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from reformists' commitment to correcting inequality, though classical reformism is silent.

public-money-creation.rationale: Public money creation is a monetary-reform idea not taken up by reformist doctrine, which accepts existing banking with regulation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bernstein: no general collapse near; capitalism adjusts through credit, cartels and world market.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Reformist internationalism has no programme of cultivating imperial legacies, though Bernstein accepted colonial acquisition.

delink-world-market.rationale: Bernstein held general stagnation is avoidable with world market extension, and reformists favour integration with regulation.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Bernstein said wage earners are heterogeneous and gain from reforms but rejected labour aristocracy theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal rights for all members of the community are core to Bernstein's democracy, so a right to discriminate is rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Bernstein supported equal rights limiting majority rule.

decide-locally.rationale: Bernstein favoured strengthening municipalities and democratic self-government while accepting that central institutions remain necessary, so subsidiarity is welcome but not absolute.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Reformism sees the democratic state as a servant of society and has no doctrine of strengthening it against hostile neighbours; Bernstein warned against bureaucracy and centralisation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Bernstein praised the superiority of organisation over anarchic competition and built his programme on association and cooperation.

recall-officials.rationale: Bernstein favoured democratic self-government but never made recall of officials a reformist demand; parliamentary reformists differ on it.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Reformists respect lawful settlement but Bernstein also criticised colonial rule; inferred as split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bernstein ties socialism to democracy and universal suffrage, which implies elected rather than hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Bernstein defends democracy as majority rule under law; a minority veto would block reform by the ballot.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Lawful means are central, but resisting a ruler who breaks constitutional law is inferred as acceptable.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Reformism works through parliaments elected by universal suffrage as the lever of change.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the humanitarian outlook of the centre-left mainstream.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream social-democratic acceptance of regulated animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Reformists base welfare on rights and solidarity rather than charity, but accept that the better-off owe obligations through taxation; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Reformism rests on active participation by citizens, parties and unions in public affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Marxist critique of culture as pacifier is more typical of revolutionary and critical-theory strands; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Bernstein stressed democratic gains eroding class rule, while later strands accept some hegemony arguments; inferred as split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not a reformist theme; Bernstein favoured colonial tutelage and trade over dependency theory; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Bernstein insists on equal rights for all citizens, which rules out reserving offices by birth.

party-own-road.rationale: Reformists reject direction by a foreign party and stress national conditions; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream social democracy favours international cooperation and aid; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Bernstein criticised nationalism and favoured peaceful arbitration over war; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal citizenship and universal suffrage exclude ancestry-based political leadership; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Later social democracy opposed fascism and wrote it into postwar settlements; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Social democrats rejected both fascism and communist dictatorship; inferred from rejection of the dictatorship of the proletariat.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; the centre-left mainstream holds slavery was the main cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Centre-left opinion is split between preservation with context and removal; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal-opportunity universalism favours attention to all disadvantaged groups; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection for all victims fits the universalist outlook; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Bernstein treats democracy and suffrage as universal; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Bernstein favours citizen armies under civil control, not a political role for the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Welfare-state social democracy supports recognising care work through benefits and wages; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: reformist social democrats are indifferent to this cultural question.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: merit-based civil service is standard in reformist state-building.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred: reformists are split between market openness and protection of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the centre-left liberalism on family law and equal rights.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Bernstein defends representative parliamentary democracy and universal suffrage, not binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Reformism builds on public welfare provision and a mixed economy, so individual private accounts would undermine it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: Bernstein backs municipal enterprise but accepts private property, not use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Bernstein's strategy rests on parliament and suffrage, and budget approval is a core parliamentary power.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from Bernstein's rejection of nationalist exclusion in favour of equal rights.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Bernstein's internationalism and liberal equal-rights stance.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: modern social democrats accept equal-outcomes tests in anti-discrimination law.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: reformism favours growth and affluence for workers, though some strands criticise consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from Bernstein's critique of colonial adventures and his preference for citizen armies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: Bernstein's defensive citizen-army stance rejects imperial intervention.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the social-democratic concern with democratic control of economic power; the sources do not discuss lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic, internationalist stance of reformist social democracy, which sees such limits as hostile to open civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The sources do not address birth rates; social democrats are split between family subsidies and immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the reformist commitment to universal citizenship rights and open societies, though municipal land policy is part of the tradition.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from social democracy's goal of full employment through state action, though Bernstein did not propose an employer of last resort.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from reformism's faith in democratic institutions and international cooperation.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Reformists work through law and parliament, so they generally hold that democratic law binds, though they accept civil disobedience in rare cases.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the social-democratic internationalist tradition that accepts limits on sovereignty, for example to stop atrocities.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the labour movement's tendency toward broad industrial unions, though Bernstein's sources do not take a position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Reformism, as a democratic and universalist tradition, rejects such conspiracy claims; inferred, as the sources do not discuss them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream social-democratic view that marriage is a legitimate institution with rights attached.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from reformism's commitment to democratic accountability of government.

local-production.rationale: The sources do not address local production; social democrats favour trade with regulation.

informal-organisation.rationale: Reformism works through lasting parties, unions and cooperatives, as Bernstein argues in the cited chapters on democracy and socialism.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist social-democratic tradition, which accepts international law and courts as constraints.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred from reformism's secular, universalist, democratic citizenship.

missingStatements.text: Socialism can be achieved through gradual reforms within existing democratic institutions rather than by overthrowing them.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim of reformist socialism, which existing statements on revolution and gradual change only partly capture.

missingStatements.text: Universal suffrage and parliamentary majorities are the proper means of transforming the economic order.
missingStatements.rationale: Bernstein calls universal franchise the alternative to violent revolution.

notes: Revolutionary Marxists who use reforms tactically (Luxemburg's critique) would answer differently, as would centre-right reformists. Many social-issue answers are low-confidence inferences from the modern centre-left.
